questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with proximal muscle weakness, periorbital edema with a violaceous discoloration of the eyelids. Which condition is most likely associated with this finding?
questions.exp: The violaceous discoloration of the eyelids described is the classic heliotrope rash, a pathognomonic finding in dermatomyositis. It is often accompanied by proximal muscle weakness and elevated muscle enzymes.

questions.q: A 22-year-old woman with no prior HPV vaccination presents for counseling. She has been sexually active since age 18. Which statement regarding HPV vaccination in this patient is most accurate?
opts: Vaccination will clear her existing HPV infections
She requires a 2-dose schedule as per CDC guidelines
She requires a 3-dose schedule (0, 1-2, and 6 months)
Vaccination is contraindicated after sexual debut
questions.exp: According to CDC/ACIP guidelines, individuals aged 15 to 26 require a 3-dose series administered at 0, 1-2, and 6 months. HPV vaccines are strictly prophylactic and do not treat pre-existing infections, but vaccination is still recommended as it protects against vaccine types the patient may not yet have acquired.

questions.q: A dermatologist is examining a patient with pediculosis and notes that the crab louse (Pthirus pubis) cannot infest the scalp despite being found on eyelashes and axillary hair. Which anatomical feature of this louse best explains this limitation?
opts: Smaller body size preventing adequate blood meal extraction
First pair of legs being too slender for hair attachment
Large pincer-like claws on second and third leg pairs adapted only for coarse, widely-spaced hair
Absence of the haustellum required to penetrate scalp skin
questions.exp: Pthirus pubis has a distinctive morphology with large, heavy, pincer-like claws on its second and third pairs of legs, which are designed to grip coarse, widely spaced hairs. These claws cannot grasp the fine density of scalp hair, restricting infestation to pubic, axillary, chest, beard, and eyelash regions.

questions.q: A 32-year-old man presents with recurrent erythematous scaly patches over the nasolabial folds, eyebrows, and scalp. Microscopic examination of skin scrapings reveals lipophilic yeast forms. Which of the following metabolites produced by the causative organism is primarily responsible for triggering inflammation in this condition?
questions.exp: Seborrheic dermatitis is associated with Malassezia species which hydrolyze sebaceous lipids. Oleic acids, generated from sebum by Malassezia lipases, are the main triggers for inflammation, and individual sensitivity to these chemicals determines disease expression.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man develops flaccid blisters and erosions after being on D-penicillamine for rheumatoid arthritis for 14 months. Direct immunofluorescence shows intercellular IgG deposits in the upper epidermis. Which pemphigus variant is most commonly associated with D-penicillamine-induced pemphigus?
questions.exp: D-penicillamine is the most common cause of drug-induced pemphigus, most commonly inducing pemphigus foliaceus or pemphigus erythematosus, with a PF to PV ratio of 4:1. The drug's sulfhydryl groups interact with desmogleins, disrupting cellular adhesion.

questions.q: Dutcher bodies, which are eosinophilic intranuclear pseudoinclusions seen in plasma cells, are characteristically:
opts: True nuclear inclusions that are PAS negative
Cytoplasm invaginated into nucleus, PAS positive and diastase resistant
Viral inclusions seen in herpes infection
Nuclear fragments that are diastase sensitive
questions.exp: Dutcher bodies are NOT true nuclear inclusions but represent cytoplasm invaginated into the nucleus of plasma cells. They are PAS positive and diastase resistant, commonly seen in lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma and multiple myeloma.

questions.q: A 3-year-old child presents with recurrent pneumonia (4 episodes in the past year), persistent oral thrush, and a deep-seated skin abscess caused by an unusual organism (Aspergillus). According to the SPUR criteria, which pattern of infections should raise suspicion for primary immunodeficiency?
opts: Single episode of viral upper respiratory infection
Serious, Persistent, Unusual, and Recurrent infections
Seasonal allergic rhinitis with secondary sinusitis
questions.exp: The SPUR mnemonic (Serious, Persistent, Unusual, Recurrent) is a clinical tool to identify warning signs of primary immunodeficiency. This child demonstrates all four features: serious (pneumonia), persistent (thrush), unusual (Aspergillus), and recurrent (multiple episodes).

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman with AIDS presents with progressive visual loss. Fundoscopy reveals hemorrhages with white perivascular exudates described as 'pizza pie' or 'cottage cheese and ketchup' appearance. Her CD4 count is most likely:
questions.exp: CMV retinitis typically occurs at CD4 counts <50 cells/µL, representing profound immune depletion. This threshold is also associated with disseminated MAC, PML, and primary CNS lymphoma.

questions.q: A 28-year-old HIV-positive male presents with severe, widespread seborrheic dermatitis involving the face, scalp, and chest that is poorly responsive to topical therapy. At what CD4 count level does seborrheic dermatitis typically manifest in HIV patients?
questions.exp: Seborrheic dermatitis in HIV patients typically occurs at a mean CD4 count of more than 400 cells/μL, making it an early cutaneous manifestation of HIV disease. Its prevalence and severity increase with worsening immunosuppression.

questions.q: A 32-year-old HIV-positive male presents with painful vesicular eruptions along the T10 dermatome. He has no other complaints and physical examination reveals no oral lesions or significant weight loss. His CD4 count is 380 cells/µL. According to WHO clinical staging, this patient is classified as:
questions.exp: Herpes zoster is a characteristic finding of WHO Clinical Stage 2 (Mild) HIV disease. Other Stage 2 manifestations include moderate weight loss (<10%), seborrhoeic dermatitis, papular pruritic eruptions, and fungal nail infections.

questions.q: A researcher is studying the immune evasion mechanisms of Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Which component of the gonococcal cell wall, when modified by host-derived molecules, provides resistance to complement-mediated bactericidal activity of normal human serum?
questions.exp: Neisseria gonorrhoeae possesses lipo-oligosaccharide (LOS) rather than LPS. Sialylation of LOS using host CMP-NANA provides profound resistance to complement-dependent bactericidal action of normal human serum, enabling survival and dissemination into the bloodstream.

questions.q: A placenta from a stillborn fetus shows enlarged, pale, and thickened placenta with club-shaped villi. The umbilical cord shows severe inflammation with a characteristic 'barber pole' appearance. What is this umbilical cord finding called, and what does it indicate?
opts: Wharton's jelly deficiency; fetal growth restriction
questions.exp: Necrotizing funisitis is severe inflammation of the umbilical cord classically described as having a 'barber pole' appearance and is a hallmark of fetal systemic response to congenital syphilis. It strongly correlates with poor fetal outcomes and indicates transplacental spread of Treponema pallidum.

questions.q: Which of the following clinical scenarios best exemplifies the 'U' component of the SPUR warning signs for primary immunodeficiency?
opts: Streptococcal pharyngitis in a school-age child
Disseminated Mycobacterium avium complex infection in an infant
Acute otitis media following upper respiratory infection
questions.exp: The 'U' in SPUR stands for Unusual infections, which include opportunistic pathogens like Mycobacterium avium complex, Pneumocystis jirovecii, or invasive fungal infections that are not typically seen in immunocompetent individuals.

questions.q: A 52-year-old man undergoes complete lymph node dissection for Stage IIIB melanoma with BRAF V600E mutation. His pathology reveals 4 involved lymph nodes with extracapsular extension. He inquires about adjuvant systemic therapy options. Which statement regarding his adjuvant treatment is most accurate?
opts: Ipilimumab monotherapy provides superior relapse-free survival compared to nivolumab
Dabrafenib plus trametinib for 12 months demonstrated approximately 58% 3-year relapse-free survival in COMBI-AD trial
Anti-PD-1 therapy is contraindicated in BRAF-mutated melanoma
Adjuvant radiotherapy to the nodal basin improves overall survival in his scenario
questions.exp: The COMBI-AD trial demonstrated that 12 months of combined BRAF/MEK inhibition (dabrafenib + trametinib) achieved an estimated 3-year RFS of 58% compared to 39% for placebo in high-risk Stage III BRAF V600-mutated patients. Anti-PD-1 agents have superseded ipilimumab due to better safety profiles, and nodal basin radiotherapy improves local control but not overall survival.

questions.q: A middle-aged man with chronic, asymptomatic reddish-brown plaques on the glans penis showing 'cayenne pepper spots' is diagnosed with Zoon's balanitis after biopsy. He has failed multiple courses of topical corticosteroids. What is the definitive curative treatment for this condition?
questions.exp: Circumcision is the gold standard and definitive curative treatment for Zoon's balanitis as it removes the occlusive environment of the foreskin that perpetuates the condition. Medical therapies including topical steroids and calcineurin inhibitors provide temporary relief but rarely achieve lasting cure.

questions.q: A 58-year-old male presents with a recurrent basal cell carcinoma on the nasal ala. Histopathology shows a morpheaform pattern. Which characteristic of this tumor subtype makes Mohs micrographic surgery the preferred treatment modality?
opts: Rapid superficial spread with minimal depth invasion
Iceberg phenomenon with clinical margins underestimating subclinical extent
Well-circumscribed borders allowing easy margin assessment
questions.exp: Morpheaform/sclerosing BCC commonly displays the 'iceberg phenomenon' where clinical margins grossly underestimate the true subclinical extent. This, combined with the H-zone location (nose), makes MMS mandatory for complete tumor clearance with tissue conservation.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman with Wilson disease on long-term D-penicillamine therapy for 12 years presents with asymptomatic keratotic papules arranged in a serpiginous pattern on her neck. Histopathology shows transepidermal elimination of abnormal elastic fibers with thickened bundles displaying prominent lateral protrusions. What is the characteristic histopathological description of these elastic fiber changes?
questions.exp: D-penicillamine-induced elastosis perforans serpiginosa shows transepidermal elimination of abnormal elastin with a pathognomonic 'bramble-bush' or 'lumpy-bumpy' appearance due to thickened elastic bundles with prominent lateral protrusions. This occurs with long-term use, typically over 10 years.

questions.q: A 48-year-old woman with metastatic melanoma presents with three asymptomatic brain metastases detected on staging MRI. Her tumor is BRAF wild-type. Which treatment approach has demonstrated intracranial objective response rates of 46-57% in such patients?
questions.exp: The combination of nivolumab plus ipilimumab has demonstrated remarkable intracranial efficacy with objective response rates of 46-57% in patients with asymptomatic brain metastases, often achieving durable long-term survival. WBRT is declining due to lack of efficacy and neurotoxicity, and BRAF-targeted therapy is not applicable in BRAF wild-type tumors.

questions.q: A 28-year-old male presents with purulent urethral discharge. Gram stain shows gram-negative diplococci within neutrophils. Which virulence factor of the causative organism specifically prevents phagolysosome fusion and enables intracellular survival within neutrophils?
questions.exp: PorB is the major outer membrane porin of Neisseria gonorrhoeae that translocates into host cell membranes and prevents phagolysosome fusion, activation, and degranulation inside neutrophils, enabling intracellular survival. It also mediates serum resistance by interfering with complement activation.

questions.q: A 7-year-old uncircumcised boy is brought by his parents with inability to retract the foreskin. Examination shows ivory-white sclerotic changes on the glans and inner prepuce. Which of the following statements is TRUE regarding this condition in males?
opts: Perianal involvement is characteristically seen in a figure-of-eight pattern
The condition is termed Balanitis Xerotica Obliterans
HLA-DQ7 association is stronger in males than females
questions.exp: Male genital lichen sclerosus is eponymously called Balanitis Xerotica Obliterans (BXO). Unlike females, perianal involvement is strictly spared in males, and the condition exclusively affects uncircumcised males.

questions.q: A 45-year-old homeless man presents with generalized pruritus and excoriations predominantly on the trunk. On examination, no lice are found on the body or scalp, but linear excoriations are noted on the back and shoulders. Where should the physician look to find the causative organism and its eggs?
opts: Scalp hair shafts in the occipital region
Seams and fibers of the patient's clothing
questions.exp: Pediculus humanus corporis (body louse) does not live on the human body; it resides and lays eggs in the seams and fibers of clothing, coming to the skin only to feed. This infestation is strongly associated with poor hygiene and homelessness.

questions.q: A 3-year-old child presents with diffuse erythema and superficial desquamation following a localized staphylococcal infection. A frozen section of peeled skin is obtained. Which histopathological finding would confirm Staphylococcal Scalded Skin Syndrome rather than Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis?
opts: Subepidermal split with full-thickness epidermal necrosis
Cleavage within or just below the stratum granulosum
Dense band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at the dermoepidermal junction
questions.exp: In SSSS, the cleavage occurs superficially within or just below the stratum granulosum due to exfoliative toxin action on desmoglein-1, showing only the horny layer with minimal inflammation. In contrast, TEN shows full-thickness epidermal necrosis with subepidermal split.

questions.q: A 14-year-old girl receives her first dose of HPV vaccine. She is scheduled for her second dose 6 months later. Which component of the vaccine is responsible for the robust antibody response without causing infection?
opts: Inactivated whole HPV particles containing viral DNA
Virus-Like Particles composed of self-assembled L1 capsid protein
Recombinant viral DNA integrated into yeast plasmids
questions.exp: HPV vaccines contain Virus-Like Particles (VLPs) formed by self-assembly of the L1 major capsid protein expressed through recombinant DNA technology. These VLPs are morphologically identical to native virions but contain no viral DNA, making them highly immunogenic yet completely non-infectious.

questions.q: A 6-week-old infant born to an untreated mother presents with profuse blood-tinged nasal discharge, hepatosplenomegaly, and refuses to move his lower limbs. X-ray of the lower limbs shows bilateral symmetric destruction of the medial upper tibial metaphyses. What is this characteristic radiographic finding called?
questions.exp: The Wimberger sign is a classic radiographic finding in early congenital syphilis, characterized by bilateral symmetric localized destruction of the medial upper tibial metaphyses. The Wegner sign (celery stick/saw-tooth metaphysis) represents osteochondritis. The infant's refusal to move limbs suggests pseudoparalysis of Parrot due to painful bone involvement.

questions.q: A 58-year-old postmenopausal woman presents with severe vulvar pruritus and dyspareunia. Examination reveals ivory-white, atrophic plaques with a 'cigarette-paper' texture involving the vulva and perianal region in a figure-of-eight pattern. Which autoantibody is most likely to be detected in this patient?
questions.exp: The clinical description is classic for vulvar Lichen Sclerosus. Circulating IgG autoantibodies against Extracellular Matrix Protein 1 (ECM-1) are found in approximately 80% of patients with lichen sclerosus.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with recurrent blistering lesions on her skin and mucous membranes. Immunofluorescence studies reveal autoantibodies targeting the basement membrane zone. The major laminin isoform in the cutaneous basement membrane zone, which may be a target in acquired blistering disorders, is composed of which chain combination?
questions.exp: Laminin 332 (α3β3γ2), previously known as laminin 5, epiligrin, kalinin, or nicein, is the major laminin within the cutaneous basement membrane zone. It plays a critical role in dermal-epidermal adhesion and can be a target in autoimmune blistering diseases.

questions.q: A 62-year-old uncircumcised man presents with a well-demarcated, glistening, reddish-orange plaque on the glans penis with symmetrical involvement of the inner prepuce. Biopsy shows epidermal atrophy with loss of rete ridges and a dense band-like infiltrate of plasma cells. Which histological feature is characteristically seen in this condition?
opts: Civatte bodies at the dermoepidermal junction
questions.exp: Zoon's balanitis characteristically shows diamond-shaped or 'lozenge keratinocytes' separated by uniform intercellular spaces described as 'watery spongiosis,' along with plasma cell-rich infiltrate and hemosiderin deposition. Munro microabscesses are seen in psoriasis, Civatte bodies in lichen planus, and corps ronds/grains in Darier disease.

questions.q: Which laminin isoform is the primary component of dermal microvascular basement membranes but is absent or minimally present in the epidermal basement membrane?
questions.exp: Laminin 111 (α1β1γ1), also known as laminin 1 or EHS laminin, is a primary component of dermal microvascular basement membranes with little or none found in the epidermal basement membrane, demonstrating tissue-specific distribution of laminin isoforms.

questions.q: A 45-year-old diabetic patient presents with a non-healing leg ulcer for 3 months. Which specimen collection technique is most appropriate to accurately identify the causative bacterial pathogen?
opts: Superficial swab from the ulcer surface
Deep tissue biopsy using a 3-mm curette
questions.exp: Deep tissue biopsy using a 3-mm curette is the gold standard for chronic ulcers as it accurately reflects the bacterial burden and disrupts biofilms. Superficial swabs may only isolate colonizing surface bacteria rather than true pathogens.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (DFSP) on the trunk. During Mohs micrographic surgery, which immunohistochemical marker is most commonly used to augment margin assessment?
questions.exp: DFSP forms extensive, unpredictable finger-like projections extending far beyond clinical margins. CD34 immunohistochemistry is commonly used during MMS to help identify residual tumor cells and ensure complete margin clearance, significantly reducing recurrence rates.
